title: Germany's far-right AfD scores landslide win in eastern state vote
subhead: The far-right Alternative for Germany won a landslide victory in Saxony-Anhalt state, located in the ex-communist east, taking at least 44% of the vote according to exit polls by two public broadcasters. But it is too early to tell whether they will have enough votes for an absolute majority to govern the state alone.

title: The end of a lawless paradise? Local government seeks to take back control of Corsican islet
subhead: Cavallo, a little gem of the Lavezzi archipelago, has always sparked envy. Once the scene of wild parties, it drew the international jet set before becoming a target for nationalists and organized crime groups. In June, the local government launched an offensive to regain control of the port and open the island up to tourists.

title: Business is booming for social run clubs
subhead: The rapid rise of these informal urban running groups, which offer a range of free services, is being strongly driven by the running ecosystem, which sees them as potential consumers in a market that grew by 17% in France in 2025.

title: The letters from two Ukrainian sisters: 'Stay in bed or take shelter elsewhere: a life-or-death decision'
subhead: Sasha and Olga Kurovska are two Ukrainian sisters, one lives in Kyiv, the other in Paris. Faced with Russian strikes on civilian infrastructure, Sasha admires her fellow citizens' determination to never give up, while Olga, fresh from a month-long stay in Ukraine, better understands her sister's reactions to the constant threat of bombing.

title: French left renews push to raise inheritance taxes, from forced philanthropy to wealth transfer cap
subhead: From the CFDT trade union to presidential candidates Raphaël Glucksmann and Marine Tondelier, the idea of increasing inheritance taxes is back on the table. The far-right Rassemblement National opposes it. Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu is considering another option: compulsory philanthropy for large inheritances.

title: Frida Kahlo's paintings, the wealthy collector and her cunning friend spark a fight for Mexico's art
subhead: On September 8, part of the most important collection of modern Mexican art assembled by Jacques and Natasha Gelman will be exhibited in Spain. The future of this priceless collection now lies with the Spanish bank Santander. In Mexico, a collective fears that these paintings, considered national heritage, may never be displayed in their home country again.
